newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures slump by close as storm fear recedes.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures slump by close as storm fear recedes.

text.p: Fears that Hurricane Fran would wreak havoc to orange growing areas receded, leaving a market without a prop as funds and speculators moved in to sell, pushing FCOJ sharply lower by close.
The National Hurricane Center said Hurricane Fran was moving towards northwest Bahamas, and it was expected to turn gradually further northwest.
The Center expected Fran to touch the U.S. in northern Florida or North Carolina during Thursday or Friday.
Floor traders said speculative and fund sell stops were triggered. "There was no support underneath the market," a floor source said.

Judy Ganes of Merrill Lynch said there was also long fund liquidation as the market softened. "I would think we are going to see good trade support coming in - I don't think the market is going to continue its freefall," Ganes said.
November orange juice settled 6.75 cents lower at 107.10 cents per lb, traded 114.25 to 105.00 cents in good volume.
September, which closed 1.45 cents off at 116.65 cents, escaped heavy losses because there were no delivery notices issued for that month, Ganes noted.
